serpentora.title: What Serpentora is for
serpentora.short: Keeps the record of your collection: each animal, its genetics and logs, your pairings from the first lock to the hatchlings, and the care around them.
serpentora.more: Everything is organised by species. Open a species from the Dashboard to see its animals, its pairings, the Breeding Advisor and its family tree. Feed Prep, Spaces, Quarantine, the Calendar and Lab tests cover the whole collection, whatever the species.
tips: New here? Press ? and choose a guided tour. It has you do each thing once, for real.
Not sure what a button does? Press ?, then Explore the app, then press the button. Nothing happens except an explanation.

main-nav.title: Navigation
main-nav.short: Moves between the parts of Serpentora. Nothing is lost when you switch.
main-nav.more: Animals, Breeding, Breeding Advisor and Family Tree belong to one species, so they appear once a species is open. The rest cover the whole collection. On a phone the same places sit in the bar at the bottom, and the less used ones are under More.
tips: Keyboard: Tab moves along the tabs, Enter opens one.

nav-dashboard.short: Shows every species you keep, with totals, and closes the species that is open.
nav-dashboard.more: Start here. Each species card opens that species. The search on the Dashboard looks through every animal in every species.

nav-animals.short: Lists the animals of the open species, as cards or as a table.
nav-animals.more: Add, find, filter and open animals here. With no species open, it asks you to pick one first.

nav-pairings.short: Follows the pairings of the open species, from planning to hatchlings.
nav-pairings.more: Each pairing is a card that moves through its stages: locks, ovulation, pre-lay shed, eggs, incubation and hatch. With no species open, it asks you to pick one first.

nav-advisor.short: Suggests pairings toward a goal you set, from the animals you have.
nav-advisor.more: The suggestions are estimates worked out from the genetics recorded on your animals. With no species open, it asks you to pick one first.

nav-family-tree.short: Shows an animal's parents, grandparents and offspring.
nav-family-tree.more: Parentage is read from what you recorded on each animal and pairing. With no species open, it asks you to pick one first.

nav-feed-prep.short: Opens a list of which feeders to thaw for the animals you pick.
nav-feed-prep.more: It covers the whole collection, not only the species that is open. It opens as a window over the current screen.

nav-spaces.short: Lays out your rooms, racks and terrariums, and which animal lives where.

nav-quarantine.short: Tracks animals in quarantine: how long they have been in, their checks and when they are cleared.
nav-quarantine.more: The number on the tab is how many animals are in quarantine right now.

nav-calendar.short: Shows feeds, locks, due dates and other events by month.

nav-lab-tests.short: Collects genetic test orders for your animals and shows the past orders and their results.
nav-lab-tests.words: genetic tests shed test lab orders terminal

nav-setup.short: Holds your breeder details, ID format, exports, appearance, language, backups and account.

nav-more.short: On a phone, opens the places that do not fit in the bottom bar: Breeding Advisor, Quarantine, Family Tree, Spaces and Lab tests.

species-gate.title: Open a species first
species-gate.short: Appears when you open a screen that belongs to one species and none is open yet. Pick a species to go on.
species-gate.more: Picking a species from the list opens it on the screen you asked for. If you have no species yet, it offers to add an animal or import a collection instead.

saving.title: How saving works
saving.short: What you change is saved in this browser as you go. There is no Save button for the collection itself.
saving.more: While you are signed in, your changes are also sent to your Serpentora account on the server shortly after you make them, so another device signed in to the same account can fetch them. If sending fails, a Not synced note appears at the top. Forms that edit one animal or pairing keep nothing until you press their own Save button.
tips: Settings, Backups lets you download a full copy to a file whenever you want one.
saving.words: save autosave storage sync where data stored

help-button.title: Help & Manual
help-button.short: Opens the Help menu: explore the app, read the manual, or take a guided tour.
help-button.more: The ? sits in the top bar on every screen, and every window has its own ? in its header. Inside a window, its ? turns Help Mode on or off directly.
tips: Keyboard: Tab to the ? and press Enter.

help-mode.title: Help Mode
help-mode.short: While it is on, pressing any control explains it instead of using it. Nothing is changed.
help-mode.more: Turn it on with ?, then Explore the app. A note at the bottom of the screen shows it is on, with an Exit button. Typing, pasting and saving are all stopped while it is on, so you can press anything safely. Turning it on pauses a guided tour; you can resume the tour from the Help menu.
tips: Keyboard: Tab to a control and press Enter or Space to hear about it. Escape closes an explanation.
Press Exit in the note at the bottom, or press ? and choose Exit Help Mode. Inside a window, its own ? leaves Help Mode directly.
help-mode.words: explore explain what does this do safe

help-manual.title: Help Manual
help-manual.short: Lists every explanation in Serpentora by section, with a search.
help-manual.more: Each entry is the same text Help Mode shows for that control. Links inside an entry open related entries; Back returns to the one before.

manual-search.title: Search the manual
manual-search.short: Finds entries whose words start with what you type.
manual-search.more: Every word you type must match the start of a word in the entry, so "pair" finds "pairing". Titles count most, then other names for the same thing, then the descriptions. Clear the search to return to where you were.

guided-tours.title: Guided tours
guided-tours.short: Walk you through Serpentora by having you press the real controls, one step at a time.
guided-tours.more: A tour points at a control and waits until you have used it. It never acts for you, apart from one plainly labelled offer to add an example animal, and it only explains deleting, importing, syncing, ordering and anything that leaves the app. Exit any time; the Help menu keeps your place so you can resume.
tips: Escape inside the tour panel leaves the tour.
Alt+G brings you back to the tour panel from anywhere.
guided-tours.words: tour guide walkthrough tutorial onboarding learn

help-hint.title: Help hint
help-hint.short: A small note pointing at the ? button. Dismiss it once and it stays away.

tour-invitation.title: Get to know Serpentora
tour-invitation.short: Offers the essentials tour on your first visit. Start it now or choose Not now; it is offered only once.
tour-invitation.more: You can start the tour later from the ? button.

scroll-top.title: Scroll to top
scroll-top.short: Jumps back to the top of the page. It appears once you have scrolled down.

dashboard-screen.title: Collection totals
dashboard-screen.short: Counts every animal you keep, how many species they belong to, and how many pairings are still active.
dashboard-screen.more: The Dashboard is the one screen that looks across the whole collection. Below the totals, each species has a card, and the Breeding table shows which species need you this week. While the example animals are showing, they are counted too.

dashboard-demo.title: Demo
dashboard-demo.short: Marks the example animals that fill an empty collection, so the app has something to show.
dashboard-demo.more: The examples disappear as soon as you add or import a real animal of your own. If you later delete your last real animal, the examples come back. Species made only of examples are shown faded.

dashboard-add-animal.short: Opens the form to add one animal by hand, in any species.
dashboard-add-animal.more: You choose the species in the form. A species gets its own card on the Dashboard once you keep an animal of it, so a new species appears here after you save its first animal.
tips: Adding your first real animal hides the example animals.

dashboard-import.short: Opens the import, which reads many animals from a file instead of typing each one in.
dashboard-import.more: It takes a CSV file or a spreadsheet, including the CSV file you can export from your MorphMarket account. The import window walks you through each step.
dashboard-import.words: csv spreadsheet excel morphmarket upload file bulk

dashboard-search.short: Finds animals in every species at once, by name, ID, genes, tags or group.
dashboard-search.more: You do not need to open a species first. While you type, the results replace the rest of the Dashboard. Every word you type must match. Up to 25 results are listed; if there are more, type more to narrow it down.
tips: This search is separate from the one on the Animals screen, so a word typed here never filters a species list.

dashboard-search-clear.title: Clear search
dashboard-search-clear.short: Empties the search box and brings the Dashboard back.

dashboard-search-result.title: Search result
dashboard-search-result.short: Opens this animal's record, inside its own species.
dashboard-search-result.more: Each result names its species, because two animals with the same name can live in different species. Opening one also opens that species.

dashboard-species.short: Lists the species you keep, one card each, with the most animals first.
dashboard-species.more: A species appears only once you keep an animal of it. The full list of species to choose from is in the form for adding an animal.

dashboard-species-card.title: Species card
dashboard-species-card.short: Opens this species, on its Animals screen.
dashboard-species-card.more: The top half counts the animals: females, males, unsexed, and the common statuses. The bottom half shows breeding: active pairings, fertile eggs, how many pairings sit at each stage, and the most pressing date coming up. Red means overdue, amber means due within three days.

dashboard-breeding.short: Shows, for every species at once, how many pairings are overdue, due soon, due next week, or being tracked.
dashboard-breeding.more: The counts are the same ones the Breeding screen shows, worked out the same way. Press a number to open that species' Breeding screen showing only those pairings. A zero has nothing behind it, so it does nothing.

dashboard-breeding-species.title: Species name
dashboard-breeding-species.short: Opens this species' Breeding screen with every pairing showing.

dashboard-breeding-overdue.short: Counts pairings whose next expected step is already past its date. Press the number to see them.

dashboard-breeding-due.short: Counts pairings whose next step is due within three days. Press the number to see them.

dashboard-breeding-soon.short: Counts pairings whose next step falls within the next seven days. Press the number to see them.

dashboard-breeding-tracking.short: Counts every active pairing in this species. Press the number to open its Breeding screen unfiltered.
dashboard-breeding-tracking.more: Tracking is the total, not a separate group: it includes the overdue and due pairings.

animals-scope-bar.title: Open species
animals-scope-bar.short: Names the species that is open, with how many animals you keep of it and how many genes Serpentora knows for it.
animals-scope-bar.more: Animals, Breeding, the Breeding Advisor and the Family Tree all show only this species while it is open. The bar stays visible so you always know which species you are adding to.

animals-all-species.short: Closes the open species and goes back to the Dashboard.
animals-all-species.more: Nothing is lost. Open any species again from its card on the Dashboard.

animals-screen.title: Animals
animals-screen.short: Lists the animals of the open species that match your filters, with how many there are.
animals-screen.more: The heading says which view is showing (All animals, Males or Females) and counts the animals that pass the search and filters, not the whole species.

animals-view.title: All, Males, Females
animals-view.short: Shows every animal of the open species, only the males, or only the females.
animals-view.more: Animals whose sex is not set appear under All only. Your search and filters apply on top of this choice.

animals-groups-view.short: Switches to the Groups view, where you create and delete groups and see who is in each.
animals-groups-view.more: The search box and the list controls hide in this view, because they only filter the animal list.

animals-layout.title: Cards and List
animals-layout.short: Draws the animals as cards, or as one table row each.
animals-layout.more: Cards show recent care and breeding cycles, and let you log a new entry from the activity tiles. List fits more animals on screen, sorts by pressing a column heading, and can be saved as a CSV file. The choice is remembered in this browser.

animals-sort.short: Puts the animals in order by name, sex, status, weight, last feed, price or date added.
animals-sort.more: Default order is the order the animals are stored in, usually the order they were added. Choosing a field always starts ascending; use the arrow beside it to reverse. Your choice is remembered in this browser.

animals-sort-direction.title: Ascending or descending
animals-sort-direction.short: Reverses the sort order, between ascending and descending.
animals-sort-direction.more: It does nothing while Default order is chosen.

animals-export-csv.short: Saves the animals listed right now as a CSV file you can open in a spreadsheet.
animals-export-csv.more: Only the animals that pass your search and filters are saved, in the order shown. The file has name, ID, sex, genetics, status, weight, last feed, groups, tags and pairings. Nothing in Serpentora changes. It shows only in the List layout.

animals-actions.short: On a phone, opens the list of animal actions: add an animal, import, export QR labels and scan a QR code.
animals-actions.more: On a wider screen the same four actions sit at the right of the toolbar instead.

animals-add.short: Opens the form to add one animal to the species that is open.
animals-add.more: The new animal is filled in with the open species. Nothing is added until you finish the form. Adding your first real animal hides the example animals.

animals-import.short: Opens the import, which reads many animals from a CSV file or spreadsheet at once.
animals-import.more: It also reads the CSV file you can export from your MorphMarket account. The import window walks you through each step.
animals-import.words: csv spreadsheet excel morphmarket upload bulk

animals-export-qr.short: Opens a window that makes a PDF of QR labels, one per animal, to print and stick on enclosures.
animals-export-qr.more: Scanning a label with Scan QR, or with a USB scanner on this screen, opens that animal's record.
animals-export-qr.words: labels print tags qr codes pdf

animals-scan-qr.short: Opens the scanner, which reads an animal's QR label and opens its record.
animals-scan-qr.more: You can use the device camera, a USB scanner, a photo of the label, or paste the code by hand.

animals-scanner-status.title: Scanner ready
animals-scanner-status.short: Shows that a USB scanner can be used on this screen without opening anything first.
animals-scanner-status.more: While the animal list is showing, a scan typed in by a USB scanner opens the animal with that ID. The note then says which animal opened, or that no animal has that ID. It is a status, not a button.

animals-search.title: Search
animals-search.short: Narrows the list to animals whose name, ID, genes, tags or group contain what you type.
animals-search.more: Every word you type must match somewhere. It searches only the open species and works together with the other filters. Status is not searched: use the Status filter for that.
animals-search.words: find filter morph het name id

animals-search-clear.title: Clear search
animals-search-clear.short: Empties the search box so the whole list shows again.

animals-status-filter.title: Status filter
animals-status-filter.short: Shows only the animals with the status you pick, such as Breeder, Holdback or Sold.
animals-status-filter.more: One status at a time. Choose No status at the top of the list to stop filtering by status.
animals-status-filter.words: tag status filter breeder holdback sold

animals-status-clear.short: Stops filtering by status. Group filters stay as they are.

animals-status-delete.short: Deletes this status from your list of statuses, and removes it from every animal that has it.
animals-status-delete.more: There is no confirmation and no undo: the animals keep everything else but are left with no status. Set a new status on each one in its record if you need to.

animals-group-filter.title: Group filter
animals-group-filter.short: Shows only the animals in the groups you tick. With nothing ticked, every group shows.
animals-group-filter.more: Tick more than one group to see the animals of all of them together. On a phone the same groups are in the Filters sheet.

animals-group-filter-clear.short: Unticks every group and shows unassigned animals again. A status filter stays as it is.

animals-hide-unassigned.short: Hides the animals that are not in any group.
animals-hide-unassigned.more: Press again to show them. It works together with the group filter.

animals-filter-sheet.short: On a phone, opens a sheet with the group filters and Hide unassigned. The number counts the filters that are on.
animals-filter-sheet.more: Filters take effect as soon as you tap them. The Status filter stays on the screen itself, above this button.

animals-filter-chip.title: Active filter
animals-filter-chip.short: Shows a filter that is on. Tapping a group or Hide unassigned chip turns that filter off.
animals-filter-chip.more: Tapping a status chip does not turn the status filter off at the moment. Use Clear filters in the Filters sheet, or No status in the Status filter, instead.

animals-filter-sheet-clear.short: Turns every filter off: groups, Hide unassigned and the status filter.

animals-filter-sheet-apply.short: Closes the Filters sheet. Your choices already took effect when you tapped them.

animals-gene-colors.title: Gene colors
animals-gene-colors.short: Shows or hides the key to the colours used for genes on the cards and in the list.
animals-gene-colors.more: Each colour stands for a kind of gene: recessive, het or possible het, super, incomplete dominant, dominant, or other.

animals-card.title: Animal card
animals-card.short: Sums up one animal: photo, name, ID, hatch date, sex and genetics, its latest care, status and pairings.
animals-card.more: Use Edit to open the full record. The coloured tiles show the last feed, weight, cleaning, shed and medication, and pressing one logs a new entry. Females with breeding history also list their breeding cycles by year.

animals-edit.short: Opens this animal's full record, where you change its details, logs, photos and parentage.
animals-edit.more: Changes in the record are kept only when you press its Save button.

animals-pair.short: Starts a new pairing with this animal already chosen as the male or the female.
animals-pair.more: Pairing picks parents from the Breeders group. If this animal is not in it, Serpentora first asks whether to move it there; an animal has one group, so it leaves its current group, and the move stays even if you then cancel the pairing. The pairing itself is created only when you finish the pairing form.

animals-more.short: Opens more actions for this animal: open its family tree, or delete it.

animals-family-tree.short: Opens the Family Tree with this animal in the middle, showing its parents and offspring.
animals-family-tree.more: Parentage comes from what is recorded on the animals and their pairings.

animals-delete.short: Deletes this animal, after you confirm.
animals-delete.more: Every pairing this animal is part of is deleted with it. There is no undo in the app. The deletion is saved in this browser and, while you are signed in, also sent to your Serpentora account shortly after. A backup file made before the deletion still holds the animal.

animals-order-test.short: Opens a window to pick gene tests for this animal at a lab and add it to a batch order, or save the test for later.
animals-order-test.more: Adding to the batch sends nothing yet: a Batch Order panel appears, and you review and send the batch from there. Save for later keeps the test in a queue on your Serpentora account instead. The tests offered come from the chosen lab's own list.

animals-activity-tile.title: Activity tiles
animals-activity-tile.short: Shows the latest feed, weight, cleaning, shed and medication logged for this animal. Press one to log a new entry of that kind.
animals-activity-tile.more: Only kinds that already have an entry show a tile. To log a first entry, use Edit and the animal's logs. The Group tile only shows the animal's group and does nothing when pressed.
animals-activity-tile.words: logs feed weight shed cleaning meds quick log

animals-breeding-cycles.short: Lists this female's breeding cycles by year, with the lock, ovulation, pre-lay shed, egg and hatch dates recorded. Open shows the pairing.

animals-card-pairings.short: Lists up to three pairings this animal is part of. Press one to open it on the Breeding screen.
animals-card-pairings.more: If there are more, a +more button opens the full list in a window.

animals-table-pairings.title: Pairings
animals-table-pairings.short: Opens a window listing every pairing this animal is part of. The number counts them.

animals-sort-header.title: Column headings
animals-sort-header.short: Sorts the list by this column. Press the same heading again to reverse the order.
animals-sort-header.more: Animal, Status, Weight and Last feed can be sorted. The sort here and the Sort by menu are the same setting.

animals-quick-add.title: Quick add
animals-quick-add.short: Logs one new feed, weight, cleaning, shed or medication entry for this animal without opening its record.
animals-quick-add.more: The entry is added when you press Add, and saved like every other change. A feed remembers the feeder you chose, so the next quick feed starts from it. Change or delete entries later in the animal's logs.

animals-quick-add-date.short: The day the entry happened. It starts as today.

animals-quick-add-feed-type.short: The kind of feeder: mouse, rat or multimammate. Changing it clears the weight class.

animals-quick-add-size.short: The feeder's size class, such as pinky or adult. The choices depend on the feed type.

animals-quick-add-feeder-weight.short: The feeder's weight in grams, if you weighed it. It is not remembered for the next feed.

animals-quick-add-form.short: How the feeder was offered: live, freshly killed, frozen/thawed or other.

animals-quick-add-form-detail.short: Describes the method when Form is set to Other.

animals-weight-chart.short: Draws the last twelve weights logged for this animal, with the latest weight and the change since the first one shown.

animals-quick-add-drug.short: The name of the medication given.

animals-quick-add-dose.short: How much was given, written your way, for example 0.1 ml.

animals-quick-add-notes.short: A short free note kept with this entry.

animals-quick-add-refused.short: Logs the feed as refused: the animal did not take it.
animals-quick-add-refused.more: The entry keeps the date and the feeder you offered, marked as refused.

animals-quick-add-save.short: Adds the entry to this animal's logs and closes the window.

animals-quick-add-close.title: Close or Cancel
animals-quick-add-close.short: Closes the window without adding anything.

animals-close.title: Close or Cancel
animals-close.short: Closes this window without doing anything else.

animals-pairings-window.title: Pairings for an animal
animals-pairings-window.short: Lists every pairing this animal is part of, with its start date and appointments.

animals-pairings-open.short: Opens this pairing on the Breeding screen.

animals-export-qr-window.title: Export QR to PDF
animals-export-qr-window.short: Makes a PDF with one QR label per animal, each 100 mm by 50 mm, ready to print.
animals-export-qr-window.more: Choose all animals, the animals in some groups, or animals you tick. All snakes means every animal in every species, not only the open one. The PDF is saved to your device; nothing in Serpentora changes.

animals-export-qr-all.short: Makes a label for every animal you keep, in every species.

animals-export-qr-groups.short: Makes labels only for the animals in the groups you tick.

animals-export-qr-selected.short: Makes labels only for the animals you tick in the list.

animals-export-qr-generate.short: Builds the PDF of labels and saves it to your device.
animals-export-qr-generate.more: If nothing is chosen, it asks you to choose at least one animal first.

animals-qr-preview.title: QR for an animal
animals-qr-preview.short: Shows one animal's QR code with its ID and genetics, ready to download as a picture.
animals-qr-preview.more: No button in the app opens this window at the moment. Use Export QR for labels.

animals-qr-download.short: Saves this QR code to your device as a PNG picture.

animals-scan-window.short: Reads an animal's QR label and opens that animal's record.
animals-scan-window.more: Choose the device camera or a USB scanner. You can also upload a photo of the label, or paste the code into the box. If no animal has that ID, it says so.

animals-scan-camera.short: Uses this device's camera to read the label. Your browser asks for permission the first time.
animals-scan-camera.more: The choice between camera and USB scanner is remembered in this browser.

animals-scan-usb.short: Turns the camera off and readies the box below for a USB scanner, which types the code in for you.
animals-scan-usb.more: The choice between camera and USB scanner is remembered in this browser.

animals-scan-camera-view.title: Camera view
animals-scan-camera-view.short: Shows the camera picture. Hold the label inside the box until it is read.
animals-scan-camera-view.more: Good light and a steady hand help. If the camera is blocked, upload a photo of the label instead.

animals-scan-upload.title: Upload image
animals-scan-upload.short: Reads the QR code from a photo or screenshot of a label.
animals-scan-upload.more: If the code cannot be read, try a sharper, well lit photo.

animals-scan-input.short: Takes a scanned or pasted QR code. Press Enter or Lookup to open the animal.

animals-scan-lookup.short: Opens the animal whose code is in the box.

animals-groups-screen.title: Groups
animals-groups-screen.short: Lists your groups, how many animals each holds, and who they are.
animals-groups-screen.more: An animal is in one group at a time. You put an animal in a group from its record. The Breeders group is the one pairing and the Breeding Advisor pick parents from.

animals-group-new.title: New group
animals-group-new.short: Creates a group with the name you type. Press Add to create it.
animals-group-new.more: A name that already exists is not added twice. The group is empty until you put animals in it from their records.

animals-group-delete.title: Delete group
animals-group-delete.short: Deletes an empty group straight away, without asking.
animals-group-delete.more: A group that still has animals cannot be deleted: move those animals to another group first, from their records. No animal is deleted.

animals-group-add-inline.title: Add new group
animals-group-add-inline.short: Creates a new group with the name you type and puts this animal in it when you save the form.
animals-group-add-inline.more: An animal is in one group at a time, so it leaves its current group.

animals-breeders-gate.title: Breeders group
animals-breeders-gate.short: Explains why pairing or the Breeding Advisor cannot suggest anything yet: the Breeders group needs at least one male and one female.
animals-breeders-gate.more: Pairing and the Advisor only pick parents from the Breeders group. Nothing is put there for you, because the app cannot tell a breeding adult from a holdback.
animals-breeders-gate.words: breeders group empty no male no female

animals-breeders-choose.short: Opens a list of your sexed animals that are not in the Breeders group yet, so you can choose which to move there.

animals-breeders-add-animal.title: Add an animal
animals-breeders-add-animal.short: Opens the form to add an animal, because none you keep could fill the missing place in the Breeders group.
animals-breeders-add-animal.words: add a male add a female

animals-breeders-select-all.title: Select all males or females
animals-breeders-select-all.short: Ticks every male, or every female, in the list. Press again to untick them.

animals-breeders-pick.title: Animal to move
animals-breeders-pick.short: Ticks this animal to move it into the Breeders group.
animals-breeders-pick.more: If it is in another group now, the row says which one. An animal has one group, so it would leave that group.

animals-breeders-add.short: Moves the ticked animals into the Breeders group, where pairing and the Advisor can use them.
animals-breeders-add.more: Each one leaves its current group. To undo, change the group back in each animal's record.

animals-acquisition.title: Acquired from
animals-acquisition.short: Shows where this animal came from when it was transferred to you through a Serpentora Market sale: the seller, the genetics they recorded and how each was known, and any lab certificates.
animals-acquisition.more: It appears only on animals that arrived with such a record. A gene marked Predicted or Observed was not tested.

animals-acquisition-certificate.short: Opens this certificate's page in a new tab.

animals-repro.short: Sums up this female's breeding history from her recorded pairings: cycles, locks, intervals between stages and fertility, with date estimates for what comes next.
animals-repro.more: It is worked out on the Serpentora server from the pairings already sent to your account, so it needs you to be signed in. The predicted dates are estimates with a range, based on her own history or, without enough of it, on averages. The more complete seasons she has, the better they get.
animals-repro.words: reproductive female cycles ovulation prediction fertility

animals-repro-refresh.short: Loads the reproductive summary again, to include pairing changes made since it was opened.

animals-repro-tabs.title: Overview, Cycles, Predictions
animals-repro-tabs.short: Switches between her summary, her cycles one by one, and the predicted dates for her current cycle.

animals-repro-cycle.title: Cycle
animals-repro-cycle.short: Opens or closes the details of one breeding cycle: its stage dates, the days between them, lock dates and fertility.

record-window.title: Animal record
record-window.short: Shows and edits everything recorded about one animal: its details, genetics, photos, parentage, sale details and logs.
record-window.more: Edits in this window are a draft. Nothing in the form is kept until you press Save changes, and Cancel throws the draft away. A few things act at once and are not undone by Cancel: Delete, taking or uploading a photo, Set as cover and Remove in the photo window, Publish to Marketplace, adding or deleting a status, and creating a new group. Open family tree closes the window without saving.
tips: Press Save changes before you open the family tree, or the edits in the form are lost.
record-window.words: edit animal details card profile snake record

record-save.short: Keeps every change in the form and closes the window.
record-save.more: The animal is then saved in this browser, and while you are signed in it is also sent to your Serpentora account shortly after. If you changed the ID, its pairings, its offspring's parent links and its place in Spaces follow the new ID. If For Sale is on, saving also publishes or updates its Marketplace listing; if For Sale was turned off on a published animal, saving takes the listing back to a draft. When the Marketplace cannot be updated, the animal is still saved and a message says so.

record-cancel.short: Closes the window and throws away the changes in the form.
record-cancel.more: Things that already acted at once stay as they are: photos you added, Set as cover, removed photos, a Publish to Marketplace, statuses you added or deleted and new groups.

record-delete.short: Asks you to confirm, then removes this animal from your collection.
record-delete.more: It acts at once, not on Save changes. Every pairing that includes this animal is removed with it. There is no undo inside the app; a backup file you downloaded earlier is the only way back.

record-family-tree.short: Closes this window and opens the Family Tree centred on this animal.
record-family-tree.more: The window closes without saving, so any changes in the form that you have not saved are lost.

record-export-pdf.short: Downloads a PDF sheet for this animal with your breeder details, its details, genetics and logs.
record-export-pdf.more: It uses what is in the form right now, including changes you have not saved yet. For a female it also lists her breeding cycles. If it fails, a message says Export failed.

record-qr-label.short: Downloads a PDF label with a QR code for this animal's ID, its name and genetics.
record-qr-label.more: It needs an ID, so the button is off until the animal has one. Scanning the code later in Serpentora opens this animal.
record-qr-label.words: qr label tub sticker print scan

record-status.short: Sets the animal's status, such as Active, Holdback, For sale, Sold or Quarantine.
record-status.more: A status says what the animal is to you right now, and the Animals list can filter by it. Choosing Quarantine here, or choosing another status for an animal in quarantine, moves it in or out of the Quarantine section when you save. Choosing No status saves it as Active.
tips: The For sale status is a label for your own lists. The For Sale switch further down is what a Marketplace listing follows.
record-status.words: tag status label state holdback sold

record-status-add.short: Creates a new status from the text you typed and gives it to this animal.
record-status-add.more: The new status joins the list straight away for every animal. Giving it to this animal is kept only when you press Save changes.

record-status-delete.short: Deletes this status from the list and clears it from every animal that has it.
record-status-delete.more: It acts at once, with no confirmation and no undo, and it is not stopped by Cancel. Animals that had it are left with no status.

record-name.short: The animal's name as it shows on cards, labels and lists.
record-name.more: A hatchling named in the form Dam x Sire, as the hatch wizard names them, has its parents read from the name when the window opens, if they are not set yet.

record-id.short: The animal's unique ID, used on labels, in QR codes, and to link pairings and offspring.
record-id.more: You can type one by hand. If you change it and save, pairings, offspring and Spaces follow the new ID. An ID that marks the sex, such as 26-U-242, changes its letter when you change the sex, unless the new ID is already used by another animal.

record-generate-id.short: Fills in an ID from your ID format in Settings, when the field is empty.
record-generate-id.more: It is off while the animal already has an ID. It uses the name, sex, genetics and birth year, and skips IDs already in use.

record-update-id.short: Builds a fresh ID from your ID format and puts it in the field, replacing the current one.
record-update-id.more: Use it after changing the name, sex, genetics or birth date, or your ID format. The new ID is kept only when you press Save changes.

record-sex.short: Records the animal as Male, Female or Unknown.
record-sex.more: Pairing picks males and females by this field. If the ID marks the sex, its letter follows the change.

record-species.short: Sets which species the animal belongs to, which decides its gene list and where it is listed.
record-species.more: Changing the species clears the genes recorded on the animal, because genes belong to one species. You are asked to confirm first when it has genes. An animal recorded before species were tracked shows as Ball Python until you correct it.

record-birth-date.short: The hatch or birth date. A full date, a year and month, or only a year are all accepted.

record-genetics.short: Records the animal's morphs and hets. Type a gene name or alias, then pick the form you mean from the list.
record-genetics.more: Each gene is offered in the forms it can take: a recessive as visual, het, 66% het, 50% het or possible het; a codominant as the single gene, its super where one exists, or possible; other genes as the gene or possible. Click the x on a chip to remove it, or press Backspace in the empty box to remove the last one. The list is the open species' gene table, so it stays off until a species with morph data is chosen. Pairing odds are worked out from what you record here.
tips: Typing 66 clown or super pastel jumps to that form in the list.
record-genetics.words: morphs hets genes traits genetics alleles

record-weight.short: The animal's current weight in grams.
record-weight.more: This is the single figure shown on the card. Weight history over time lives in the Weights log below.

record-feed-cycle.title: Feed Cycle
record-feed-cycle.short: Records what this animal eats and how often, for Feed Prep and the Calendar.
record-feed-cycle.more: Feed Prep uses the food type and size to list which feeders to thaw. With an interval set, the Calendar shows the next feed as due that many days after the last feed that was not refused.

record-feed-type.short: The kind of feeder this animal takes, such as mouse or rat.

record-feed-size.short: The feeder size this animal takes. The choices depend on the food type.

record-feed-weight.short: The feeder weight in grams, if you go by weight rather than size class.

record-feed-quantity.short: How many feeders this animal gets per feed.

record-feed-interval.short: How many days between feeds. The Calendar shows the next feed as due this many days after the last accepted feed.
record-feed-interval.more: No reminder appears until the animal has at least one feed log that was not refused.

record-feed-notes.short: A short note about preparing this animal's food, shown with its Feed Prep entry.

record-group.short: Puts the animal in one of your groups, or in none.
record-group.more: An animal is in one group at a time. Pairing and the Breeding Advisor only offer animals in the Breeders group. The change is kept when you press Save changes.

record-add-group.short: Creates a new group with the name you typed and puts this animal in it.
record-add-group.more: The group joins this species' group list straight away. In the edit window, putting this animal in it is kept only when you press Save changes.

record-photo-take.short: Opens the camera, where the device has one, and adds the picture to this animal.
record-photo-take.more: The photo is added and becomes the cover at once, without waiting for Save changes. Photos are shrunk before they are stored.

record-photo-upload.short: Adds one or more pictures from your files to this animal.
record-photo-upload.more: They are added at once, without waiting for Save changes, and the last one becomes the cover. Photos are shrunk before they are stored.

record-photo-view.short: Opens all of this animal's photos, where you can open, set the cover or remove each one.

record-photo-clear.short: Takes the cover picture off the card, without deleting any photo.
record-photo-clear.more: It is kept only when you press Save changes. With no cover chosen, the most recent photo is shown in its place.

record-gallery.title: Photos
record-gallery.short: Lists every photo stored for this animal, with where it came from, its size and when it was added.
record-gallery.more: Changes here act at once, even while the edit window behind it is open.

record-gallery-open.short: Opens the photo full size in a new tab, where you can also save it.

record-gallery-set-cover.short: Makes this photo the one shown on the animal's card and record.
record-gallery-set-cover.more: It acts at once. The current cover shows Current cover instead.

record-gallery-remove.short: Asks you to confirm, then deletes this photo from the animal.
record-gallery-remove.more: It acts at once and cannot be undone. If it was the cover, the most recent remaining photo takes its place.

record-parentage.short: Records the animal's dam and sire, either from a tracked clutch or picked by hand.
record-parentage.more: The Family Tree is drawn from these links. Linking a clutch fills in both parents and locks the pickers; unlinking keeps the parents it filled in. The changes are kept when you press Save changes, or when you press Add for a new animal.
record-parentage.words: parents dam sire mother father lineage

record-clutch.short: Links the animal to a clutch from your pairings, which fills in its dam and sire.
record-clutch.more: Only clutches recorded under Breeding are listed. A clutch ID recorded earlier that matches no tracked clutch is still kept and shown.

record-dam.short: Picks the mother from your females. Breeders are listed first.
record-dam.more: A dam that has left the collection keeps her recorded name, marked as not in collection. The picker is off while a clutch is linked.

record-sire.short: Picks the father from your males. Breeders are listed first.
record-sire.more: A sire that has left the collection keeps his recorded name, marked as not in collection. The picker is off while a clutch is linked.

record-pairing-overview.short: Lists the pairings this animal is part of, with its partner, the number of appointments and the current stage.
record-pairing-overview.more: It is read only. Pairings are changed under Breeding.

record-logs.short: Holds the animal's history: feeds, weights, sheds, cleanings and meds.
record-logs.more: New entries, edits and deletions here are part of the draft, kept only when you press Save changes.

record-log-add.short: Adds a new entry dated today to this log, ready to fill in.
record-log-add.more: A new feed entry starts from the feeder, size and method you used last, never from the last weight.

record-log-delete.short: Removes this entry from the log.
record-log-delete.more: There is no confirmation. The removal is part of the draft: Cancel brings the entry back, Save changes makes it final.

record-feeds.short: Records each feed: date, feeder, size, weight, how it was offered and a note.
record-feeds.more: The last feed that was not refused is what the Feed Cycle reminder counts from.

record-mark-refused.short: Marks this feed as refused, so it no longer counts as a meal.
record-mark-refused.more: A refused feed is skipped by the feed reminder. Undo refused turns it back into a normal feed.

record-undo-refused.short: Turns a refused feed back into a normal feed entry.

record-weights.short: Records weigh-ins over time: date, grams and a note.

record-sheds.short: Records each shed by date, whether it came off in one piece, and a note.

record-cleanings.short: Records enclosure cleanings by date, whether it was a deep clean, and a note.

record-meds.short: Records treatments: date, drug, dose and a note.

record-delete-dialog.title: Delete animal
record-delete-dialog.short: Asks you to confirm before an animal is removed from your collection.
record-delete-dialog.more: Deleting also removes every pairing that includes the animal. There is no undo inside the app. The example animals are only shown until you add or import a real animal.

record-delete-confirm.short: Removes the animal and every pairing that includes it.
record-delete-confirm.more: This cannot be undone inside the app. A backup file you downloaded earlier is the only way to get it back.

record-delete-cancel.short: Closes this question and keeps the animal.

concept-morph.title: Morph
concept-morph.short: A morph is a named gene or look an animal carries, such as Pastel, Clown or Piebald.
concept-morph.more: In the hobby, morph is used both for a single gene and for the combination an animal shows, like Pastel Clown. In Serpentora each gene is recorded on its own, in the form the animal has it: visual, het, possible, or super. The genetics list badges each gene R for recessive, Co for codominant, D for dominant, P for polygenic, L for locality and Ph for a physical trait.

concept-visual.title: Visual
concept-visual.short: A visual animal shows the gene in its looks. For a recessive gene that means it carries two copies.
concept-visual.more: A visual recessive, such as a Clown, passes one copy to every baby. A codominant or dominant gene is visual with a single copy. A gene marked possible, such as Possible Pastel, means you are not sure the animal has it at all; it is kept as a note and left out of pairing odds.

concept-het.title: Het
concept-het.short: Het means the animal carries one hidden copy of a recessive gene. It looks normal for that gene but can pass it on.
concept-het.more: Each baby of a het parent has a 50% chance of getting the copy. Two hets for the same gene give, on average, about one visual in four babies, but each egg is its own chance, so a clutch can have more or none. Serpentora treats a plain Het as certain when it works out pairing odds.

concept-possible-het.title: Possible het, 66% het and 50% het
concept-possible-het.short: A possible het may or may not carry the gene. The percentage is the chance that it does.
concept-possible-het.more: Normal looking babies from two hets are each 66% het, meaning a two in three chance. Babies from a het and a non carrier are each 50% het. Possible Het without a number is counted as a 50% chance. Pairing odds use these chances, so a prediction from a possible het is lower than from a proven one. Only breeding the animal, or a lab test, proves it.
concept-possible-het.words: possible het 66% 50% pos het probable carrier odds

concept-super.title: Super
concept-super.short: A super is an animal with two copies of a codominant gene, such as a Super Pastel.
concept-super.more: A super passes one copy to every baby. Some supers have a trade name, shown after the gene, such as Super Mojave being a Blue Eyed Leucistic. Genes whose super form is lethal are never offered as a super. Leucistic animals are recorded by the genes that make them, which is why entering BEL asks which genes.

concept-status-vs-group.title: Status and group
concept-status-vs-group.short: A status says what an animal is to you now; a group says which set of animals it belongs to.
concept-status-vs-group.more: Status is a label like Active, Holdback, For sale, Sold or Quarantine, used for filtering and for moving animals in and out of quarantine. A group is a set like Breeders or a rack, and an animal is in one group at a time. Pairing and the Breeding Advisor only use the Breeders group. Neither one publishes anything: a Marketplace listing follows the For Sale switch alone.

add-window.short: Adds one animal to your collection: pick its species, fill in what you know, then press Add.
add-window.more: Only the species and one other detail are required. When you press Add the animal is saved in this browser, and while you are signed in it is also sent to your Serpentora account shortly after. Adding your first real animal hides the example animals.

add-close.short: Closes the window without adding the animal.

add-species.short: Picks the animal's species. It is required, and it decides which genes the genetics field offers.
add-species.more: Changing the species clears any genes already picked. Species marked no morph data have no gene table, so genetics cannot be recorded for them yet.

add-quick-add.short: Takes a pasted line about the animal, such as an ID, sex, genes, weight and birth year, so Update Fields can read it into the form.
add-quick-add.more: Write sex as 1.0 for male and 0.1 for female. A species named at the start of the line, like crested gecko, is used if no species is picked.
add-quick-add.words: paste free text quick add line

add-update-fields.short: Reads the Quick Add text into the empty fields of the form.
add-update-fields.more: It only fills fields that are still empty and never adds the animal by itself. Breeder and feeding details it finds go into the notes. If the text names a leucistic, it asks which genes make it.

add-name.short: The animal's name. A name in the form Dam x Sire fills in the parents when they match animals you have.

add-id.short: An ID of your own, if you want one. Left blank, an ID is made from your ID format.
add-id.more: If the ID you type already exists, a number is added to the end to keep it unique.

add-sex.short: Records the animal as Male, Female or Unknown.

add-status.short: Picks the animal's starting status. With none picked it is saved as Active.
add-status.more: Choosing For sale shows a Price field. It does not publish anything.

add-genetics.short: Records the new animal's morphs and hets. Type a gene name or alias, then pick the form you mean.
add-genetics.more: The list is the chosen species' gene table, so it stays off until a species with morph data is picked. Click the x on a chip to remove it.

add-weight.short: The animal's weight in grams today.

add-price.short: A price for your own records. It appears when the status is For sale.
add-price.more: Adding the animal does not publish it. Listing on the Marketplace is done from the animal's record.

add-year.short: The hatch year. Typing a birth date fills it in for you.

add-birth-date.short: The hatch or birth date. A full date, a year and month, or a year alone are all accepted.

add-group.short: Puts the new animal in one of this species' groups, or in none.

add-arrival.short: Says whether the animal is a new arrival or already in your collection.
add-arrival.more: A new arrival is given the Quarantine status and a quarantine record starting today. An animal already in your collection keeps the status you picked and is not quarantined.

add-source.short: Where the new arrival came from. It sets how many days its quarantine runs.

add-source-name.short: The breeder, shop or shipment the new arrival came from, for the quarantine record.

add-cancel.short: Closes the window without adding the animal.

add-submit.short: Adds the animal to your collection and opens its species.
add-submit.more: It is off until a species and at least one other detail are filled in, or when your plan's animal limit is reached. If the genetics name a leucistic, it first asks which genes make it. For a new arrival, a short notice about quarantine may show before the animal is added.

add-species-backfill.short: Appears when some animals were recorded before Serpentora tracked species, and asks what species they are.
add-species-backfill.more: Until they have a species they are treated as Ball Python. One answer here sets all of them at once; mixed collections can be corrected per animal afterwards in each record.

add-backfill-species.short: Picks the species to give every animal that has none yet.

add-backfill-later.short: Closes this question for good, so you can set each animal's species in its own record.
add-backfill-later.more: It does not appear again in this browser.

add-backfill-apply.title: Set all to species
add-backfill-apply.short: Gives every animal without a species the one you picked, then closes this question.

add-leucistic.short: Asks which genes make the leucistic you entered, so it is recorded as genes rather than as BEL.
add-leucistic.more: A Blue Eyed Leucistic is two compatible genes from the BEL complex, such as Mojave and Lesser. A Black Eyed Leucistic is the super form of one gene. Cancel removes the leucistic word and records nothing in its place.
add-leucistic.words: leucistic bel blue eyed black eyed

add-leucistic-type.short: Chooses Blue Eyed Leucistic, made of two genes, or Black Eyed Leucistic, made of one gene's super form.

add-leucistic-bel.title: BEL Gene 1 and BEL Gene 2
add-leucistic-bel.short: The two genes that make this Blue Eyed Leucistic. They must be different genes.

add-leucistic-black.short: The gene whose super form makes this Black Eyed Leucistic. It is recorded as Super and the gene.

add-leucistic-cancel.short: Closes this window and records nothing for the leucistic.

add-leucistic-apply.short: Records the chosen genes in place of the leucistic you entered.

import-window.short: Brings many animals in at once from a MorphMarket CSV export, a spreadsheet, a PDF or pasted text.
import-window.more: Every way in shows what it found before anything is added. Imported animals are saved in this browser, and while you are signed in they are also sent to your Serpentora account shortly after. Importing hides the example animals.
tips: Import one species at a time, then check a few records before importing the next.
import-window.words: import upload bring in migrate collection

import-close.short: Closes the import window. Nothing is imported unless you pressed Import.

import-already-owned.short: Ticked, the animals come in as part of your collection and nothing is quarantined.
import-already-owned.more: Untick it for new arrivals: each one then gets the Quarantine status and a quarantine record from today. A row that already has the Quarantine status is quarantined either way.

import-source.short: Picks how your animals come in: a MorphMarket export, a generic CSV or spreadsheet, or a PDF.
import-source.more: You can also paste text into the box below instead.

import-morphmarket.short: Reads the CSV export of your animals from MorphMarket, or the same file saved as an Excel workbook.
import-morphmarket.more: The file is recognised from its header row, not its name, so there are no columns to map. Each row's species comes from its MorphMarket category, and its traits are read against that species' genes. You review every row before anything is added. A file that does not look like a MorphMarket export is refused with a message.
tips: This only brings animals in. Serpentora does not send anything to MorphMarket.

import-generic-csv.short: Reads a CSV or Excel file, matching columns such as Name, ID, Sex, Morphs and Hets from the first row.
import-generic-csv.more: The animals show in the preview; nothing is added until you press Import. A file that turns out to be a MorphMarket export switches to the MorphMarket review instead. Without recognisable column titles, columns are read in a fixed order: name, sex, genetics, groups, tags.

import-pdf.short: Reads the text out of a PDF animal list and shows the animals it found in the preview.
import-pdf.more: The text also lands in the paste box, so you can correct it and press Preview again. Scanned PDFs that are only pictures have no text to read.

import-paste.short: Takes a pasted animal list, for example text copied from a PDF, for Preview to read.
import-paste.more: One animal per line works, as do blocks of name, sex and genetics, or values separated by the | character.

import-species.short: The species given to every animal in this import. Import is off until one is picked.
import-species.more: Import one species at a time. A single animal can be corrected in its record afterwards. MorphMarket files do not use this; their species comes from each row.

import-preview.title: Preview
import-preview.short: Reads the pasted text and lists the animals it found, without adding anything.
import-preview.more: Check names, sex and genetics in the list before you import. If a line names a leucistic, it asks which genes make it.

import-cancel.short: Clears the text, file and preview, and closes the window without importing.

import-submit.short: Adds every animal in the preview to the chosen species, then opens that species.
import-submit.more: An animal with the same name and sex as one you already have is skipped. It is off until there is a preview and a species, or when your plan's animal limit would be passed. There is no undo inside the app, so download a backup first if you want a way back.

import-mm-review.title: Animals detected from MorphMarket
import-mm-review.short: Shows every row read from the MorphMarket file, with counts and any warnings, before anything is added.
import-mm-review.more: Each row is Ready, Warning, Conflict or Error. A conflict is a row whose animal ID you already have; it starts on Skip so nothing is overwritten by accident. Errors, such as a category that names no known species, cannot be imported.

import-mm-row.short: Chooses whether this row is imported or skipped. For an ID you already have, it chooses Skip or Update existing.
import-mm-row.more: Update existing changes only the fields the file fills in: name, sex, species, and genes, birth date, price and weight when the file has them. A blank cell never erases what you have. A weight is also added to the weight log, dated today.

import-mm-confirm.title: Import animals
import-mm-confirm.short: Adds the rows set to import and updates the ones set to Update existing.
import-mm-confirm.more: It is off when nothing is set to import, or when the new animals would pass your plan's animal limit; set rows to Skip until it fits. The MorphMarket price is kept as the animal's price for your records and does not put it up for sale. There is no undo inside the app.

import-mm-cancel.short: Leaves the review and closes the window without importing anything.

import-mm-result.title: Import complete
import-mm-result.short: Shows how many animals were imported, updated, skipped and failed.

import-mm-breeders.short: Offers to move the imported adults you tick into the Breeders group, which pairing and the Breeding Advisor use.
import-mm-breeders.more: Nothing is ticked for you, and you can change groups later in each record.

import-mm-view.short: Closes the window and shows the imported animals in their species.

sell-for-sale.short: Marks the animal for sale on the Marketplace and shows its price, currency and description.
sell-for-sale.more: Saving with For Sale on publishes the animal's Marketplace listing, or updates it, with its name, species, sex, birth date, genetics, price, currency, description and cover photo. Turning it off and saving takes a published listing back to a draft. If your plan does not include Marketplace listings, nothing is published and the panel says so.

sell-price.short: The asking price shown on the listing.

sell-currency.short: The currency of the price: EUR, USD or GBP.

sell-description.short: Text that goes with the listing, such as feeding, temperament or what is included.

sell-publish.short: Publishes this animal's listing on the Marketplace now, without waiting for Save changes.
sell-publish.more: It uses what is in the form now: name, species, sex, birth date, genetics, price, currency, description and cover photo. The rest of the form is still a draft until you press Save changes. If publishing fails, the reason shows above the button. When your plan does not include Marketplace listings, a notice shows here instead of the button.

sell-published.short: Says this animal has a published Marketplace listing.
sell-published.more: Saving with For Sale on keeps the listing up to date. Turning For Sale off and saving takes it back to a draft.

record-order-test.short: Opens the genetic test window for this animal, to pick a lab and the tests you want.
record-order-test.more: Opening it orders nothing. Tests you choose go into a batch; the order only goes to the lab when you submit the batch from the batch cart.

breeding-screen.title: Breeding
breeding-screen.short: Follows the pairings of the open species, from the first appointment to the hatchlings.
breeding-screen.more: The tabs at the top switch between the Dashboard, Active pairings, Completed pairings and the Incubator. Each pairing is a card holding its appointments, locks, ovulation, pre-lay shed, clutch and hatch. Everything you change on a card is saved as you go.
tips: Start with New pairing. Only animals in the Breeders group can be paired.

pairing-view-dashboard.short: Shows every active pairing as a short card with its current stage, next stage and target date.
pairing-view-dashboard.more: Use it to see what needs doing today. The counts at the top filter the cards by how soon the next step is due.

pairing-view-active.title: Active pairings
pairing-view-active.short: Lists the pairings that are still running, one card each.
pairing-view-active.more: A pairing leaves this list when you mark it completed, when its hatch is recorded, or when every egg is marked bad. The number on the tab is how many active pairings there are.

pairing-view-completed.title: Completed pairings
pairing-view-completed.short: Lists finished pairings, with filters by year and by outcome.
pairing-view-completed.more: A pairing counts as completed when you mark it completed, when its hatch is recorded, or when all its eggs were marked bad. Completed pairings keep all their records, and you can reopen one.

pairing-view-incubator.title: Incubator
pairing-view-incubator.short: Shows every recorded clutch as egg boxes, with laid and due dates and the eggs left.
pairing-view-incubator.more: Egg boxes come from the clutches logged on your pairings. A clutch of more than 10 eggs is shown as two boxes. The number on the tab is how many clutches are incubating.

pairing-search.title: Search pairings or snakes
pairing-search.short: Narrows the pairing lists to pairings whose label or parents match what you type.

pairing-search-clear.short: Empties the pairing search so every pairing shows again.

pairing-qr-labels.short: Opens a window to print QR labels for all your pairings or for the ones you pick.
pairing-qr-labels.more: You get a PDF file with one label per pairing. Each label shows the pairing, its parents and its appointment dates, and a QR code that links back to that pairing in Serpentora.

pairing-new.short: Opens the Create pairing window to pair a breeder male with a breeder female.
pairing-new.more: Only animals in the Breeders group can be chosen. A female can be in one active pairing at a time.

pairing-filter-year.title: All years
pairing-filter-year.short: Shows completed pairings from one breeding season, or from all of them.

pairing-filter-outcome.title: All outcomes
pairing-filter-outcome.short: Shows completed pairings with one kind of result, such as eggs or live birth, no ovulation observed, or follicles reabsorbed.
pairing-filter-outcome.more: Late outcome means an event was recorded after the pairing was marked completed. Reopened means the pairing was completed once and then opened again.

breeding-dashboard.title: Breeding Dashboard
breeding-dashboard.short: Sums up your active pairings: what is overdue, what is due soon, and which stage each pairing has reached.

breeding-urgency-card.title: Overdue, Due in 3 days, Next 7 days, Tracking
breeding-urgency-card.short: Counts pairings by how soon their next step is due. Press a count to show only those pairings, and press it again to show all.
breeding-urgency-card.more: The due date is the target of the next stage: the pre-lay shed window after ovulation, egg laying after the pre-lay shed, or the hatch after the clutch. Tracking is the number of active pairings.

breeding-stage-counts.title: Clutch laid, Pre-lay shed, In ovulation, Locks observed
breeding-stage-counts.short: Counts active pairings by the furthest stage each has reached.

breeding-dashboard-item.title: Pairing on the dashboard
breeding-dashboard-item.short: Shows one pairing's current stage, next stage, target date and latest lock.
breeding-dashboard-item.more: The badge shows how many days are left to the target date, or how overdue it is.

breeding-dashboard-open.title: Open details
breeding-dashboard-open.short: Opens this pairing's full card so you can record the next step.
breeding-dashboard-open.more: The button is named after the next step, such as Log ovulation or Log hatch, but it only opens the card. Nothing is recorded until you do it on the card.

incubator-screen.title: Incubator
incubator-screen.short: Lists the egg boxes from every clutch you have recorded, with their eggs and due dates.

incubator-summary.title: Clutches, Egg boxes, Total eggs
incubator-summary.short: Counts the clutches, egg boxes and eggs currently in the incubator.
incubator-summary.more: Eggs marked bad are not counted.

incubator-egg-box.title: Egg box
incubator-egg-box.short: Shows one egg box: its clutch, the dates the eggs were laid and are due, the eggs in it and the days remaining.
incubator-egg-box.more: Egg boxes are numbered across all clutches. A clutch of more than 10 eggs is split into two boxes, shown as 1 of 2 and 2 of 2.

incubator-edit-box.short: Opens the egg box to record bad eggs and notes for it.

incubator-print-card.short: Downloads a clutch card PDF for this egg box, with the parents, their genetics, the lay date and the egg count.

incubator-box-dialog.title: Egg box
incubator-box-dialog.short: Shows the details of one egg box and lets you record bad eggs and notes.
incubator-box-dialog.more: Nothing changes until you press Save egg box.

incubator-bad-eggs.short: Records how many eggs in this box went bad. The box count goes down by that number.
incubator-bad-eggs.more: If every egg of the clutch is marked bad, the clutch is shown as lost and the pairing moves to Completed pairings. Set the number back to 0 to undo it.

incubator-box-notes.short: Keeps notes about this egg box, such as egg condition or movement.

incubator-save-box.short: Saves the bad eggs and notes for this egg box and closes the window.

pairing-card.title: Pairing card
pairing-card.short: Holds one pairing: its parents, appointments, locks, breeding cycle, notes and hatchlings. Press it to open it.
pairing-card.more: The heading shows the clutch number, the egg box and the season. Every change on an open card is saved as you go; there is no Save button.

pairing-clutch-id.title: Clutch ID
pairing-clutch-id.short: Names the clutch by its parents and season, as female x male and year.
pairing-clutch-id.more: It is built from the parents' names, so renaming a parent changes it.

pairing-sire.title: Sire
pairing-sire.short: Shows the male of this pairing and his genetics. Press his name to open his record.

pairing-dam.title: Dam
pairing-dam.short: Shows the female of this pairing and her genetics. Press her name to open her record.

pairing-qr-label.short: Downloads a QR label PDF for this one pairing.
pairing-qr-label.more: The QR code links back to this pairing in Serpentora.

pairing-delete.short: Deletes this pairing at once, with all its appointments, locks, clutch and hatch records.
pairing-delete.more: There is no confirmation and it cannot be undone. Hatchlings already created from it stay in your animals. To keep the history, mark the pairing completed instead.

pairing-edit.short: Shows the male and female choices so you can swap a parent. Press Done to hide them.
pairing-edit.more: Each female can be in only one active pairing.

pairing-edit-male.short: Changes the male of this pairing. The change is saved straight away.

pairing-edit-female.short: Changes the female of this pairing. The change is saved straight away.

pairing-collapse.short: Closes this pairing card back to its one line summary.

pairing-stage-tracker.short: Shows how far this pairing has come: paired, locked, ovulated, pre-lay shed, clutch laid, incubating and hatched.
pairing-stage-tracker.more: Stages light up from what you record on the card. Paired comes from a ticked appointment and Locked from a ticked lock.

pairing-label.short: Names this pairing. It starts as female x male, and you can change it.

pairing-start-date.short: Sets the date the pairing starts. Changing it moves the first appointment and spaces the later ones a month apart.

pairing-appointments.short: Plans the dates you put the male in with the female, and records whether the pairing happened and whether you saw a lock.
pairing-appointments.more: Appointments start monthly from the start date. Ticking one or setting its date moves the later appointments to follow a month apart. They also appear in the Calendar.

pairing-generate-months.short: Replaces the appointment list with five monthly appointments.
pairing-generate-months.more: Recorded pairing dates are kept as the dates of the new appointments, but ticks, locks, lock dates and notes on the old appointments are dropped. There is no confirmation.

pairing-add-appointment.short: Adds one more appointment, a month after the last recorded pairing date, or on the start date.

pairing-appointment-done.short: Marks that the pairing on this appointment happened. Today's date is filled in if no pairing date is set.

pairing-lock.short: Marks that you saw a lock on this appointment. Today's date is filled in if no lock date is set.

pairing-date.short: Records the day the pair was actually put together. Setting it ticks the appointment.

pairing-lock-date.short: Records the day you saw the lock. Setting it ticks Lock.

pairing-appointment-notes.title: Notes
pairing-appointment-notes.short: Keeps a short note for this appointment.

pairing-appointment-remove.short: Removes this appointment at once, without asking.

pairing-notes.short: Keeps free notes for the whole pairing.

pairing-hatchlings.short: Lists the hatchlings linked to this pairing. Press one to open its record.

pairing-genetics-calculator.short: Shows or hides the genetics odds for this pairing.
pairing-genetics-calculator.more: It appears only when the parents have genetics recorded that the calculator can work with.

pairing-odds.short: Shows the chance of each outcome per hatchling, gene by gene and combined, from the genetics recorded on both parents.
pairing-odds.more: These are probabilities, not promises. A clutch can come out better or worse than the odds, and the odds are only as good as the genetics you recorded. Possible hets count with their percentage.
pairing-odds.words: odds chance probability punnett outcomes het visual

pairing-completion-reason.short: Says why the pairing is finished, such as eggs laid, live birth, or no expected offspring.

pairing-outcome-confidence.short: Says how sure you are of the outcome: confirmed, likely or unknown.
pairing-outcome-confidence.more: For eggs laid or live birth the outcome is confirmed, so this choice is locked.

pairing-completion-note.short: Keeps a note about why and how the pairing ended.

pairing-mark-completed.short: Ends active tracking of this pairing and moves it to Completed pairings, with the reason, confidence and note you chose.
pairing-mark-completed.more: Nothing is deleted. You can still record ovulation, eggs or a hatch later, and you can reopen the pairing.

pairing-reopen.short: Moves a completed pairing back to Active pairings.
pairing-reopen.more: The earlier completion is kept in its history.

pairing-reopen-add-event.short: Reopens this completed pairing so you can keep recording its events as an active pairing.
pairing-reopen-add-event.more: You do not have to reopen it. Events can also be recorded while the pairing stays completed.

breeding-cycle.title: Breeding cycle
breeding-cycle.short: Records the female's cycle on this pairing: ovulation, pre-lay shed, eggs laid and the hatch.
breeding-cycle.more: Each step sets a target for the next one: about 21 days from ovulation to the pre-lay shed, 30 days from the pre-lay shed to laying, and 60 days from laying to hatch. These are fixed rough guides, not predictions for your animal.

pairing-log-ovulation.short: Records the ovulation date and notes. Once recorded, the button reads Edit details.
pairing-log-ovulation.more: If at least three appointments fall on or before the ovulation date, appointments after it are removed.

pairing-clear-ovulation.title: Clear (ovulation)
pairing-clear-ovulation.short: Removes the ovulation record and the pre-lay shed record with it, without asking.

pairing-log-prelay.short: Records the pre-lay shed date and notes. Once recorded, the button reads Edit details.
pairing-log-prelay.more: If ovulation is recorded, the days between the two are shown.

pairing-clear-prelay.title: Clear (pre-lay shed)
pairing-clear-prelay.short: Removes the pre-lay shed record, without asking.

pairing-ovulation-dialog.short: Records the date of ovulation and any notes. Save keeps them on the pairing.

pairing-prelay-dialog.short: Records the date of the pre-lay shed and any notes. Save keeps them on the pairing.

pairing-ovulation-date.short: The day you saw ovulation. It is needed to save.

pairing-prelay-date.short: The day the pre-lay shed happened. It is needed to save.

pairing-eggs-laid.short: Records the clutch: how many fertile eggs and how many slugs were laid.
pairing-eggs-laid.more: The laying date is set to today and the hatch is expected 60 days later. You can correct the date afterwards on the card.

pairing-eggs-dialog.short: Records the number of fertile eggs and slugs. The total is saved as fertile eggs plus slugs.

pairing-egg-date.short: The day the eggs were laid. The expected hatch date follows from it.
pairing-egg-date.more: It can be edited only after the clutch is recorded.

pairing-fertile-eggs.short: How many good eggs were laid. It also caps how many hatchlings can be recorded.

pairing-slugs.short: How many slugs, the infertile eggs, were laid.

pairing-clutch-card.short: Downloads a clutch card PDF with the parents, their genetics, the laying date and the egg count.

pairing-clear-eggs.short: Wipes the clutch and hatch records of this pairing, without asking.
pairing-clear-eggs.more: The laying date, egg counts, egg box notes, bad eggs and the hatch record are all cleared. Hatchlings already created stay in your animals. It cannot be undone.

breeding-cycle-timers.short: Counts down to the next milestones of this pairing, such as the pre-lay shed window, egg laying or hatch.
breeding-cycle-timers.more: Timers start once ovulation, a pre-lay shed or a clutch is recorded. When the hatch is recorded it says the cycle is over.

breeding-countdown.title: Countdown
breeding-countdown.short: Shows one milestone: the day of the cycle, the time left or overdue, and the target date.

hatch-eggs-hatched.short: Starts recording the hatch of this clutch. You are first asked whether you logged a hatch for it before.

hatch-view-edit.short: Changes the recorded hatch. You are first asked whether you logged a hatch for this clutch before.

hatch-clear-record.short: Clears the hatch date, count and notes, without asking.
hatch-clear-record.more: Hatchlings already created stay in your animals, and logging the hatch again will not create cards for them a second time. To start the hatch over and remove those animals, use Eggs hatched and answer that you logged it before.

hatch-gate.title: Have you logged hatch before for this clutch?
hatch-gate.short: Asks whether this clutch already has a hatch logged, so hatchlings are not created twice.
hatch-gate.more: Hatchling cards are only made for hatchlings that are new to this clutch.

hatch-gate-first.title: No, this is the first hatch log
hatch-gate-first.short: Opens hatch details, and then one card for each new hatchling.

hatch-gate-again.title: Yes, I have logged hatch before
hatch-gate-again.short: Lets you choose between deleting the hatchlings made earlier and logging again, or only editing the hatch details.

hatch-redo.title: Delete the old hatchling records?
hatch-redo.short: Decides what happens to the hatchlings created earlier for this clutch.
hatch-redo.more: Only animals made by the hatch wizard for this pairing are counted. Animals you linked to the clutch yourself are never touched.

hatch-redo-delete.title: Delete hatchling records and log again
hatch-redo-delete.short: Permanently deletes the hatchling animals the wizard created for this clutch, clears the hatch record, and opens hatch logging from scratch.
hatch-redo-delete.more: The deletion also reaches your other signed in devices. It cannot be undone, so make a backup first if you are unsure.

hatch-redo-keep.title: Keep them, just edit the hatch details
hatch-redo-keep.short: Keeps the existing hatchlings and opens the hatch details. No new hatchling cards will open.

hatch-details-dialog.short: Records the hatch date, how many hatched, and notes.
hatch-details-dialog.more: After you save, the hatch wizard opens one card for each hatchling that is new to this clutch.

hatch-count.short: How many eggs hatched. It cannot be more than the fertile eggs recorded.

hatch-wizard.short: Creates an animal record for each hatchling, one at a time, linked to this pairing.
hatch-wizard.more: Each hatchling gets an ID from your ID format, the pairing's parents, and is placed in a Hatchlings group for the year. Closing the window keeps the hatchlings saved so far; the rest are not created.

hatch-id.short: The ID the hatchling will be saved with. It is made from your ID format; type to set your own.

hatch-regenerate-id.short: Makes a fresh ID for this hatchling from your ID format.

hatch-sex.short: The hatchling's sex. If the ID was made for you, it is remade to match.

hatch-weight.short: The hatchling's first weight in grams.

hatch-morph.short: The hatchling's morph and hets, typed as text. They are split into genetics when it is saved.

hatch-birth-date.short: The hatchling's hatch date. It starts as the hatch date of the clutch.

hatch-previous.short: Goes back to the previous hatchling in the wizard.

hatch-save.title: Save & next
hatch-save.short: Saves this hatchling as a new animal and moves to the next one. On the last hatchling the button reads Save hatchling.

pairing-create-dialog.short: Pairs one breeder male with one breeder female and sets the start date.
pairing-create-dialog.more: Five monthly appointments are planned from the start date. In the Calendar, appointments of the same male are spaced 3 days apart.

pairing-create-male.short: Finds and picks the male. Type a name, ID or gene to search the males in the Breeders group.

pairing-create-female.short: Finds and picks the female. Type a name, ID or gene to search the females in the Breeders group.
pairing-create-female.more: A female already in an active pairing cannot be paired again until that pairing is changed or deleted.

pairing-create-clear.short: Takes back the animal you picked so you can choose another.

pairing-create-start.short: The day the pairing starts. Appointments are planned monthly from it.

pairing-create-notes.short: Keeps notes for the new pairing, such as ultrasound size or a rotation plan.

pairing-create-add.title: New pairing
pairing-create-add.short: Creates the pairing and opens it in Active pairings.
pairing-create-add.more: It needs a male and a female. Animals of different species cannot be paired.

breeders-guard.short: Explains that only animals in the Breeders group can be paired, and offers to add this one.

breeders-guard-add.short: Moves this animal into the Breeders group and carries on with the pairing.
breeders-guard-add.more: An animal belongs to one group, so it leaves its current group.

pairing-qr-dialog.short: Chooses which pairings to print QR labels for, then makes the PDF.

pairing-qr-all.short: Prints a label for every pairing in the list.

pairing-qr-selected.short: Prints labels only for the pairings you tick below.
